title: The Power Triangle: Why Not Every Volt-Amp Becomes a Watt
topic: AC power decomposes into a real component P (watts) that does work, a reactive component Q (vars) that sloshes back and forth, and an apparent component S (volt-amps) that the source must supply. The three form a right triangle: S squared equals P squared plus Q squared, and the power factor cos phi equals P over S. Scrub the phase angle phi to watch the triangle morph.

beats.narration: An AC source can deliver volt-amps that never become watts. So where does the power go?

elements.content: Not every volt-amp does work. So what is the rest doing?

beats.narration: Drive a reactive load with a sinusoidal voltage. The current rises and falls at the same frequency, but its peaks arrive a quarter cycle late. The phase angle between the two is phi.

elements.content: Top: V(t) sine in chalk-100. Bottom: I(t) sine in amber-300, lagging by phi. Phase-difference bracket between them.

beats.narration: Project the current onto V and you get the in-phase part, which carries real power P. Project it perpendicular and you get the quadrature part, which carries reactive power Q. They live at right angles to each other.

elements.content: Current phasor I at angle -phi from voltage; dashed projections onto V (in-phase) and perpendicular (quadrature). Three formulas: I·cos phi (real), I·sin phi (reactive), and S = V·I.

beats.narration: Now sweep phi from zero to ninety degrees. The hypotenuse stays the same length — that is apparent power S. Real power P shrinks; reactive power Q grows. The power factor cos phi falls from one to zero.

elements.content: Power triangle with horizontal leg P, vertical leg Q, hypotenuse S, angle phi at origin. phi sweeps; the triangle morphs in real time. Live readouts of P, Q, S, and cos phi update each frame. A 'motor analogy' caption appears at low PF.

beats.narration: Utilities bill for apparent power. Real power lights the room; reactive power just sloshes back and forth through the wires. That is why power factor correction is worth money.

elements.content: S² = P² + Q²   ·   cos phi = P/S
improve the power factor, shrink the apparent power
